sub_units.name: String Basics & Manipulation
sub_units.content: String basics involve fundamental operations such as reversing a string, checking palindromes, counting characters, and modifying case. String manipulation includes inserting, deleting, replacing characters, and transforming strings. These operations are the building blocks for solving more complex string problems and are frequently used in interviews and real-world text processing tasks.

sub_units.name: Substring Problems
sub_units.content: Substring problems focus on identifying, extracting, and analyzing portions of a string. These problems often involve sliding window techniques, two pointers, or brute force approaches. Common tasks include finding the longest substring without repeating characters, counting substrings with certain properties, and locating substrings that match a pattern.

sub_units.name: Pattern Matching
sub_units.content: Pattern matching focuses on finding whether a pattern exists inside a string and locating its occurrences efficiently. Algorithms such as Naive Search, Rabin-Karp, Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP), and Z-algorithm help reduce time complexity compared to brute force approaches. Pattern matching is widely used in search engines, DNA sequence matching, and text editors.

sub_units.name: Palindrome Problems
sub_units.content: Palindrome problems involve strings that read the same forwards and backwards. These problems often require checking palindromes, finding palindromic substrings, or partitioning strings into palindrome segments. Techniques used include two-pointer approaches, dynamic programming, and center expansion methods.

sub_units.name: String Transformation & Encoding
sub_units.content: String transformation and encoding problems involve modifying strings into different formats or representations. Examples include run-length encoding, decoding nested encoded strings, grouping anagrams, and rearranging characters under constraints. These problems test understanding of hashing, stacks, heaps, and greedy algorithms.

s=input().strip()
start=0
max_len=1

def expand(l,r):
 global start,max_len
 while l>=0 and r<len(s) and s[l]==s[r]:
  if r-l+1>max_len:
   start=l
   max_len=r-l+1
  l-=1
  r+=1

for i in range(len(s)):
 expand(i,i)
 expand(i,i+1)

print(s[start:start+max_len])
